utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. May I ask the registrar to please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-42-A, the Prosecutor versus Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Helen Brady appearing on behalf of the Prosecution together with Mr. Xavier Tracol, and our case manager, Ms. Carmela Annik-Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am attorney-at-law Vladimir Petrovic on behalf of General Strugar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now, as usual, ask Mr. Strugar himself. Can you follow the proceedings a language you understand, and do you have any complaints about the situation in the detention unit or other health problems not related to the prothesis surgery we will discuss later in the Status Conference. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I have no objections about the Detention Unit. As for my health condition, my hip problem, it's getting worse and worse, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, sorry for interrupting the accused. If I may make a very brief remark. Since the accused, Mr. Strugar, wishes to present some details about his health problem, I would like to apply for these things to be said in private session if possible. I move that we go briefly into private session so Mr. Strugar can be given an opportunity to share all these details with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this goes without saying. Deliberately I asked only on other health conditions not related to this hip replacement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And only later on when we come back to the hip replacement we'll go until private session. But sorry, Mr. Strugar, for having interrupted you. You started to tell us something about kidney problems. Please continue. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] What I would like to share with you now is that I have asked my counsel to move that this information not be released to the public. What I would like to do is tell you about my difficulties, my various difficulties. You asked me if there was anything else in addition to my hip problem. Indeed there is. I would like to share this with you, but I would like this to be done in closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: No, we have no objection to this being in closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Let's please go to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. So nothing has changed. In particular, nothing has changed since the amended provisional Practice Direction on E-court system, and therefore I want to kindly ask with a view to both Practice Directions, whenever they come across 68 material to alert individuals, the Defence, on any such exhibits or witnesses or everything that falls in the scope of Rule 68(i), no doubt superseding paragraph (ii) of Rule 68. Then it's for me to ask you are there any other issues to be raised by the parties. The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Just to mention that since the last Status Conference we have written to the Defence advising of certain collections being placed on the EDS and certain updates to the EDS following our last meeting at the Status Conference, and I understand that the Defence is satisfied with this -- proceeding this way. We've also made one disclosure under Rule 68(i) as a matter falling within our actual knowledge. Those are the only disclosure issues that have changed since the last time that we were here in the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, precisely as my learned friend says. We did receive some documents and some notes about the interview with a potential witness in August 2002, and I must say that opposed to the previous Prosecution team that omitted throughout the trial in 2003 and 2004 to disclose this very interesting document, this Prosecution team has done so. With a three-year delay, but it's better to have it at some point rather than never. So I do appreciate what this Prosecution team has done way of this careful assessment and finding documents that can be potentially interesting and important by way of evidence in these proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Having heard your contribution, I want to alert you that Defence, if it so wants, has the duty to move for a 115 admission of new documents promptly, as soon as possible. So therefore, please recall this particular duty on your side. But I think time is of the essence right now. The first thing to do is that Mr. Strugar gets his necessary treatment for today, and we expect a filing, maybe an urgent filing out of time. It's now a quarter past three. I hope that you can do it by today, but please be extremely precise for which purposes, because we heard some different scopes, some related only to the hip replacement, other contribution also to other health treatments. So please be as clear as possible, and also repeat the time frame you indicated. I don't think it's necessary to repeat all the other reasons. In there you can refer to your previous motions. And the same goes for the Prosecution. I don't think anything has to be repeated, and maybe we can do our very best to decide on this issue already this week. However, I can't promise anything because some Judges are not in The Hague right now because they have professional commitments in New York. If there is no other point to be discussed right now, the appellate hearing stands adjourned. Thank you.
